rationale: This contact sheet shows only one visible candidate, so the portfolio cannot pass a comparative massing audit. The single mass is a compact carved/offset block with stepped upper articulation, which is understandable as a neighborhood building starting point, but it does not establish portfolio breadth or materially distinct spatial identities. Because the brief requires multiple cards with legible and non-repeating three-dimensional language, the set fails on count and on repeated-family risk by default. The next run should anchor around missing geometry families that strengthen public threshold, usable void, and upper calmness without turning into box-dominated repetition.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: single compact carved-block mass with recursive court/offset pinch and stepped upper surface; one footprint one roof family only

required_next_relations: Introduce at least 2 additional non-repeating candidate masses that keep a clear active street edge but vary the sectional strategy: one courtyard carve, one notch or split-wing relation, one lifted or terraced upper mass.
Ensure each new card changes the footprint logic and roof logic, not just the label or surface texture.
Preserve a readable west-facing public threshold and one usable void/terrace tied to mixed-use ground access.
